name: pgstream-51959fb2-blind28-ots
instr:
# pgstream gives wrong answers while configuring, copying and emitting changes — without a test suite

A tool that takes a full initial load of one server's tables into another and then keeps carrying later changes across, rewriting column values on the way if you ask it to, now gets a number of things wrong — from the moment it reads the settings you hand it to the moment it shuts down. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the servers changed and nothing about the files handed to it changed. The same runs that used to come out right come out wrong, and in several places something that used to be accepted is refused outright, or something that went wrong is reported as fine.

Starting a run from a YAML settings file goes wrong in three ways. Writing a logging level into the file and asking an already-running process to pick the file up again leaves it logging at the level it was started with; the newly written level is simply never adopted. Referring to an environment variable with the curly-brace form inside a value now yields nothing at all even when that variable is exported, so a URL or a text template written that way loses its content, while bare dollar references, doubled dollars and unclosed braces are still carried through as literal text. And a file that writes the batch limits of the write destination with unit suffixes such as 64MiB is refused outright: loading it comes back as a failure instead of with the byte counts it descr
